title: On Bubble Watch
summary:
So to discern a bubble, you can look at valuation parameters, but I've long believed
a psychological diagnosis is more effective. In normal circumstances, if an industry's or a country's securities are attracting
unusually high valuations, investment historians are able to point out that, in the past, those
stocks had never sold On a whole market, or a group of securities is blasting off, and a species idea is making
its adherence rich, few people will risk calling it out.

reader_summary.overview: This is the memo by Howard Marks, on Bubble Watch. Exactly 25 years ago today, I published the first memo that brought a response from readers after having written for almost 10 years without receiving any. The memo was called bubble.com, and the subject was the irrational behavior I thought was taking place with respect to tech, internet and e-commerce stocks.

thesis: Howard Marks argues that a bubble is defined not by quantitative calculations but by a psychological state of irrational exuberance where investors believe there is no price too high. He identifies this condition by the widespread conviction that economic improvements can last forever and the fear of missing out, noting that bubbles are marked by extreme psychology rather than specific valuation parameters.
